title: Bipartite graph
summary: A bipartite graph partitions vertices into two independent sets where every edge connects a vertex from one set to the other. This structure naturally models relations between two distinct classes of objects, such as users and items, or players and clubs. The defining property is that no odd-length cycles exist, which is equivalent to the graph being 2-colorable. Bipartite graphs are foundational in discrete mathematics and appear in diverse contexts, from social network analysis to railway scheduling and network design.

mechanisms.title: Vertex Partitioning and Edge Routing
mechanisms.explanation: Vertices are divided into two disjoint sets, U and V. By definition, every edge must originate in one set and terminate in the other; edges never connect two vertices within the same set. This routing constraint enforces the bipartite structure and enables modeling of pairwise interactions between two distinct entity types.

mechanisms.title: 2-Colorability and Odd-Cycle Exclusion
mechanisms.explanation: A graph is bipartite if and only if its vertices can be colored with two colors such that no edge connects same-colored vertices. Equivalently, the graph contains no cycle of odd length. This coloring property provides a practical test for bipartiteness and underpins many algorithmic applications.
